entity.name: Asterios Raptis
entity.description: Solo maintainer of the astrapi69 library family on the JVM. mystic-crypt and its companions crypt-api and crypt-data have been published on Maven Central continuously since 2015, under the MIT licence, with a desktop application built on top of them.

projects.name: mystic-crypt
projects.description: A cryptography library and command line tool for the JVM: it generates key pairs, converts between the key and certificate formats that tools in this space keep disagreeing about (PEM, DER, PKCS#1, PKCS#8), computes checksums and message authentication codes, and encrypts files and text through Bouncy Castle rather than hand-rolled primitives. It is the layer other projects consume from Maven Central, and the layer the desktop workbench is built on.

projects.name: mystic-crypt-ui
projects.description: The desktop application built on mystic-crypt: a workbench for the keys and secrets a developer or administrator handles every day, with an encrypted local vault as one of its functions rather than its purpose. Listed here as the dependent project where part of the funded work lands, not as the applicant.

channels.description: Bank account of the maintainer, supplied directly during the grant paperwork rather than published in this manifest.
Existing public channel for ongoing support, unrelated to the grant plans below.

plans.name: Milestone 1: a lossless KeePass (KDBX) round trip
plans.description: Importing a KDBX database and exporting it again does not return what went in: entry identity is regenerated, timestamps are replaced, history is dropped. KDBX is the interchange format for local password storage, so a tool that cannot round-trip it is a one-way door. Deliverables: identity and timestamps preserved in both directions, history preserved or refused with what would be lost named, and a round-trip test against a real KDBX file. Lands in mystic-crypt-ui, where KDBX handling lives.

plans.name: Milestone 2: keys as first-class objects in the library
plans.description: Key material is handled as opaque bytes: format, algorithm, fingerprint and certificate expiry are known to whoever wrote the file, not to the software holding it. Deliverables in the library itself: a key description model that reads those properties off the key instead of taking them on trust, the existing conversion, fingerprint and checksum operations bound to it, and an expiry query. The desktop application is the first consumer, so every project depending on mystic-crypt gains the result.
